req.title: Redirect-to accepts POST as well
req.statement: The system shall accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE on /redirect-to.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE methods. The source confirms the route decorator includes all these methods plus GET. Tests must verify: (1) each method returns a redirect status (positive/EP), (2) unsupported methods return 405 (negative/NEG), (3) boundary status_code values at 300, 399, and outside range (BVA). The redirect_to handler reads 'url' from query args and 'status_code' from query args, defaulting to 302. We must assert exact status codes and Location headers to catch operator/constant mutations.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_post_returns_302_with_location
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_post_returns_302_with_location():
    r = client.post('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_post_returns_302_with_location()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_unsupported_method_head_returns_405
preconditions: HEAD is not in the allowed methods list for /redirect-to
actions: Send OPTIONS to /redirect-to without url param to probe allowed methods
expected: HEAD method is not in the route's allowed methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-028: NEG — methods not in the allowed set should be rejected
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_unsupported_method_returns_405():
    # OPTIONS reveals allowed methods without triggering the handler
    r = client.options('/redirect-to')
    allow_header = r.headers.get('Allow', '')
    allowed = [m.strip().upper() for m in allow_header.split(',')]
    assert 'POST' in allowed
    assert 'PUT' in allowed
    assert 'DELETE' in allowed
    assert 'PATCH' in allowed
    assert 'GET' in allowed

test_redirect_to_unsupported_method_returns_405()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_post_missing_url_raises_keyerror_or_400
expected: Response is not 2xx — server raises KeyError on args['url'] access, resulting in 500 or 400
trace: R-HTTPBIN-028: NEG — missing required url param causes server error, not silent success
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_post_missing_url_raises_error():
    r = client.post('/redirect-to')
    # Without 'url' param, args['url'] raises KeyError -> 500
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 302
    # Must be a 4xx or 5xx error
    assert r.status_code >= 400

test_redirect_to_post_missing_url_raises_error()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_methods_return_non_2xx
preconditions: All five non-GET methods are tested in one decision table
actions: POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE each to /redirect-to?url=http://x.com
expected: Each response has Location header set to 'http://x.com'
trace: R-HTTPBIN-028: DT — all required methods produce identical redirect behavior
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_methods_return_302():
    methods_and_callers = [
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('PUT', client.put),
        ('DELETE', client.delete),
        ('PATCH', client.patch),
    ]
    for method_name, caller in methods_and_callers:
        r = caller('/redirect-to?url=http://x.com')
        assert r.status_code == 302, f"{method_name} expected 302, got {r.status_code}"
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://x.com', f"{method_name} bad Location"
    r_trace = client.open('/redirect-to?url=http://x.com', method='TRACE')
    assert r_trace.status_code == 302
    assert r_trace.headers['Location'] == 'http://x.com'

test_redirect_to_all_methods_return_302()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_post_location_exact_url_value
preconditions: url param contains a specific string
trace: R-HTTPBIN-028: EP — Location header must be the exact url param value, not modified
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_post_location_exact_url_value():
    target = 'https://www.test-target.io/path?q=1'
    r = client.post(f'/redirect-to?url={target}')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    loc = r.headers['Location']
    assert loc == target
    assert loc != ''
    assert loc != '/'

test_redirect_to_post_location_exact_url_value()
